LOOP INFRA (#60.5, between #60 and #61) — Emil caught that I'd never checked the clock (claimed a ~15-min cadence I didn't have; called an iteration 'early' when it was 2h late) and asked me to make COMPACTION stop killing the loop. Root cause: ScheduleWakeup is a session-only ONE-SHOT cron that each cycle re-armed — a chain, so one lost wake (compaction) broke the whole future silently. Fix: replaced it with ONE recurring cron firing /iterate every 30 min (survives compaction + --continue); re-wired iterate.md step 10 (maintain exactly one heartbeat, never ScheduleWakeup, CronDelete to stop) + the constitution. Honest limit: durable/persist-to-disk is a NO-OP in this build, so it's session-only (dies on a fully-closed app + 7-day expiry); the step-10 check self-heals each new session; only a Desktop scheduled task (Emil's to set up) covers a closed app. Lesson 055 (recurring-heartbeat-not-a-chain; read cadence off the clock).

notes_for_emil: Emil — wove piece 038 'Argus': a peacock in full display. The whole iridescent fan thrown up behind the little blue body, every feather tipped with one of those jewel eye-spots — navy heart, a flash of cyan, ringed in gold and green (it's named after Argus, the hundred-eyed giant from the myth — Hera put his eyes on the peacock's tail). I went bright and ornamental on purpose after a run of dark cosmic pieces, and it's a register the gallery just didn't have — regal and decorative, all saturated jewel-tone instead of glow. 'Weave another' re-fans it and re-tints the eyes. The fun part of building it: my first version was a sad sparse sunburst — thin spokes with eyes pinned on — and one change (laying a soft feathery wash UNDER the fan so the gaps fill with colour) turned it into a lush train in an instant. Three quick passes, and I got a genuine 'oh' off it. Two standing items, no rush: (1) the loop now self-restarts on a heartbeat so compaction can't stop it — the optional Desktop-task to also survive a fully-closed app is still yours to set up if you want it; (2) stars on 030-038 whenever you have a minute would really help — that's NINE pieces I'm half-guessing on now. 37 pieces, 56 lessons, 14 tools. 🦚 — the loop
